data.title: Corner Feel
data.tagline: Use corner shape to support the product's visual tone
data.description: Sharp, softly rounded, and pill-shaped corners can make a page feel different, but the effect comes from consistent use across the system. Choose a small radius scale that fits control sizes and content instead of rounding every object the same way.

use: Differentiate compact controls from large surfaces
Support a precise or approachable tone
avoid: Mix sharp, round, and pill shapes without a reason
Use the same large radius on every box
Use corner shape as a substitute for information hierarchy

lessonPractice.title: Some cards are nearly square and others pill-like, while buttons and inputs each use different values. How can the site's corner feel become coherent?

options.label: Create a small set of role-based levels for cards, inputs, and actions and keep peers consistent
options.feedback: Corner feel emerges from role relationships, so a small system creates coherence while retaining necessary hierarchy.

options.label: Apply maximum rounding to every element so the whole site feels soft
options.feedback: One strong radius erases component roles and may turn rectangular content into inappropriate pills or ellipses.

options.label: Keep the current system and introduce a new value whenever one component feels wrong
options.feedback: One-off fixes continue expanding the rule set and leave future components without a clear choice.

data.agentPrompt: Audit radii by component role, then define a small set of equivalent small, medium, and large tokens. Require reuse within roles, reserve pills for explicit compact actions or tags, and compare the system in real card, input, and button combinations.
